purpose: A UI component used to toggle a setting on or off with a button. It lets users turn individual features on or off to adjust display settings or personalize the application's appearance.
whenToUse: Set a setting as active or inactive (for example, in a dialog)
Clearly show the current mode or state of a setting
Apply changes that take effect immediately
Use a default switch when you need a simple on/off component with predefined icons and standard colors
Use a semantic switch when the action represents a positive or negative state
Add a descriptive label above or directly before a switch component so users understand which value it controls
whenNotToUse: Don't use for selecting multiple options or when extra steps (e.g. a Save button) are required for changes to take effect
Don't use when it's unclear which state the component is displaying — use a Checkbox instead
Don't include text inside the switch component itself — this causes localization issues
doRules: Use Semantic type (green/red) when the action represents a clearly positive or negative state
Place a label above or directly before the switch to identify what it controls
Add optional text (e.g. 'On'/'Off') when the main label doesn't fully explain active vs inactive
Provide a tooltip when no label is available to give context
Use Compact density for desktop/mouse interactions; Cozy for touch devices
dontRules: Don't include text inside the switch handle — localization breaks the component
Don't use switch when change requires a separate Save action — use Checkbox instead
Don't truncate labels if avoidable — allow wrapping; truncate only as last resort

layoutGuidance.placement: Label above or directly before the switch. Side label repositions below the switch when horizontal space is insufficient.
layoutGuidance.sizing: Compact mode: smaller height for mouse/keyboard. Cozy mode: larger for touch. Width auto.
layoutGuidance.spacing: Label wraps by default. Optional text sits after the switch on the same line.
layoutGuidance.alignment: Label above: switch pushed down when label wraps. Label to side: moves below on narrow containers.

contentGuidance.labelLength: Short and descriptive (e.g. 'Enable Notifications', 'Receive Updates'). One sentence max.
contentRules: Label must identify what the switch controls
Optional text should be a single word (e.g. 'On'/'Off')
Supports LTR and RTL reading directions
Do not embed text inside the switch handle

responsiveBehavior.XL: Full switch with label and optional text
responsiveBehavior.L: Full switch with label and optional text
responsiveBehavior.M: Label may reposition below switch if side-label cannot fit horizontally
responsiveBehavior.S: Compact → Cozy for touch; side label moves below switch on narrow containers

accessibilityGuidance.requirement: Tab: moves focus to switch. Shift+Tab: navigates backward. Spacebar or Enter/Return: toggles state.
Focused state displays an additional border around the track as a visible focus indicator.
Provide a tooltip when no visible label is present to identify what the switch controls.
SAP follows WCAG and WAI-ARIA standards. See Accessibility in SAP Fiori and Accessibility Design Tools Handbook.

incompatible: Inside Table cells when multiple options need selection — use Checkbox
When a Save action is required before the change takes effect — use Checkbox

exceptions: Semantic type overrides default on/off colors with green (positive) and red (negative) — system-defined icons cannot be changed
Hover states are not supported on touch devices
types: Default: icon inside handle, default on/off colors (gray/blue)
Switch with label: label placed above or before the switch
Switch with optional text: short text after switch explains active/inactive meaning
